about: Outcome shares, day-1 spread and realised returns on one common sample, so that a statement about how often deals break, what a closed deal pays and what a break costs rests on the same deals. Read-only export from the frozen results; aggregates only. Percentages with two decimals.

definitions.sample_filter: Core sample (signed deals without reverse mergers), all-cash consideration, usable CRSP price (deal still open at the day-1 close, pre-announcement price within 15% of the price implied by the vendor's offer and premium, day-1 spread between -50% and +100%, an exit exists), and a defined market-implied break probability (offer above the pre-announcement close). Identical to the `priced` filter of src/expected_return.py; the three samples differ only in the announcement years.
definitions.outcomes: Closed = completed. Adverse break = cancelled for a reason other than a higher competing bid. Topped = cancelled because a higher competing bid won.
definitions.spread_day1: Offer known on day 1 / close on t1 - 1, where t1 is the first trading day after the announcement date (results/crsp_prices.md). The offer is the per-share price in the announcement press release where it differs from the vendor's final offer.
definitions.return: Total return of the target share (dividends included) from the close on t1 to the exit, the field behind loss_if_break in results/deck_numbers.json. Closed deals: to the closing (CRSP delisting return; the offer paid on the closing date where CRSP has no delisting record). Adverse breaks and topped deals: to the close of the first trading day after the cancellation date. Not annualized, unhedged, before costs.
definitions.loss_to_spread: Loss = return of adverse breaks with the sign reversed; spread = day-1 spread of closed deals; both from the same sample. The ratio is computed from unrounded values; 'calculation' shows it with the two-decimal inputs.

checks: pooled_2013_2025: same rows as the ranking test in expected_return.py; deals, adverse breaks and topped deals equal results/expected_return.json (1205, 38, 17); mean return per deal (+2.27%) and mean day-1 spread (2.69%) of all deals equal the deal-weighted means of the thirds published there

test_2019_2025: same rows as the ranking test in expected_return.py; deals, adverse breaks and topped deals equal results/expected_return.json (623, 22, 6); mean return per deal (+2.62%) and mean day-1 spread (3.65%) of all deals equal the deal-weighted means of the thirds published there

spread and return columns reproduce all 6 rows of the day-1 spread table in results/crsp_prices.md (usable all-cash deals, which also include deals without a market-implied probability: deals, median and mean spread, mean return)
all_2001_2025: same filter, no published count to compare with; it contains the two samples above as subsets

pooled_2013_2025.title: Common sample: priced all-cash deals announced 2013-2025 (the ranking-test sample)
